summary.headline: Lohia Corp Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR594 crores, with order book near INR2,000 crores (up 93% YoY) and EBITDA margin at 19.4%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to INR594 crores and 18% QoQ, with H1 revenue up 50% to INR1,097 crores. EBITDA rose 33% YoY to INR116 crores, but margin eased to 19.4% from 20.7% a year earlier, which management attributed to higher commodity prices. PAT rose 48% YoY to INR77 crores, and the company reported a net cash position of INR123 crores. Order book reached about INR2,000 crores, with a record export order book, and management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 30-35%.

financial_highlights.change: +33% YoY from INR87 crores; margin vs 20.7% in Q2 FY26 and 19.9% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~INR2,000 crores (INR1,994 crores per analyst read-back, not disputed)
INR115 crores / INR238 crores; net cash INR123 crores
financial_highlights.change: Net debt to equity -0.18x; net debt to EBITDA -0.57x

segments.name: Machinery
segments.commentary: Machinery revenue was INR480 crores in Q2, about 81% of quarterly revenue.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Aftermarket (spares and services) revenue was INR50 crores in Q2; management expects spares growth to support FY28.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.commentary: Other revenue was INR59 crores in Q2. Recycling machinery is still small, at an expected INR30-35 crores for FY27, with management targeting roughly a doubling in FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 30-35% YoY; H1:H2 split expected at about 45:55, implying H2 revenue of INR1,200-1,300 crores.
Order book expected to stay in the INR2,000-2,200 crores range by March 2027.
FY28 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, implying roughly INR2,500-2,600 crores, with possible spillover of orders from FY27.
Sustainable EBITDA margin range of 19-21%; internal planning figure of 20%.
Current capacity seen as supporting revenue of about INR2,500 crores; FY27 capex around INR75 crores, with a new shed planned for assembly capacity and Kanpur land available.
Recycling machinery revenue expected to roughly double in FY28.
capex_capacity: Current capacity supports revenue of about INR2,500 crores, which may need balancing equipment in one or two plants.
FY27 capex of about INR75 crores covering maintenance, balancing, and new machine capacity for conversion, recycling, and coating machinery.
Plans to build a new shed for additional assembly capacity; Kanpur premises have land available for further expansion.
Vendor base in Kanpur, Faridabad, and Bangalore is being expanded; three dedicated ancillaries in Kanpur have added capacity.
Management said utilisation cannot be measured precisely because capacity is fungible between in-house and vendor capacity across heterogeneous products.
demand_pricing: Export order book at an all-time high, about INR500 crores plus; the company exports to over 100 countries, with a customer base mainly in the developing world.
Domestic demand traction described as heavy after two to three years of low investment, with inquiries rising from mid-2025 and expected to continue for at least five to six months.
List prices were raised in February 2026 and July 2026; orders booked after a revision are priced at new rates. Contracts with 6-9 month delivery do not get price increases in the interim.
Overall inquiry pipeline about INR13,000 crores, with historical conversion of 15-20% into firm orders.

Domestic growth drivers cited: cement bags, block-bottom bags replacing pillow bags, BOPP bags, wrapping and specialty fabric. Management expects a slight slowdown in FY28 orders as industry capacity is added and fabric conversion rates cool from peak.
Gross margin fell about 3% QoQ, mainly due to input cost inflation (commodity prices, geopolitics) and some geography mix; management said gross margin is at around 41%.
Recycling: 1-2 machines executed per month; a first ReclaMax 120 (500 kg/hr) was supplied to a domestic customer; washing lines and mother-baby recycling launched.

qa_highlights.question: Does a customer buy the full project or individual machines?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers mostly buy complete projects (tape extrusion, looms, downstream equipment); partial and balancing orders for solo looms are smaller, typically 2 to 12 machines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 19-21%, with an internal 20% planning figure, subject to commodity trends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book capacity and inquiry pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports about INR2,500 crores of revenue; inquiry pipeline is about INR13,000 crores with 15-20% conversion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is recycling and spares?
qa_highlights.answer: Machinery order book of about INR2,000 crores includes INR30-35 crores of recycling machines; spares (about INR30-35 crores of annual revenue) are excluded from the order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY28 growth expected to slow to 10-15%, and what drove domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic growth came from new conversion segments such as block-bottom bags plus fabric and cement bags; management expects slower order growth as industry capacity is added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share in converting machines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 25-35% share in converting machines, depending on the machine type.

risks_watch: Commodity (raw metal) price inflation and geopolitics: contracts lock prices for 6-9 months, so margin pressure can persist; EBITDA margin fell YoY to 19.4% in Q2.
Execution timing: customer site readiness, bank finance, and LC delays in exports can push dispatches beyond 6-9 months, and orders may spill into FY28.
Capacity ceiling near INR2,500 crores revenue; vendor capacity and balancing equipment needed to exceed it.
Expected FY28 deceleration to 10-15% growth after a 30-35% FY27 year, with domestic fabric-conversion demand cooling.
Recycling is an early-stage segment (about INR30-35 crores), with PET not a current focus and rigid recycling order book not yet established.
Balance-sheet disclosure: other current liabilities of INR478 crores, mainly customer advances (about 20% of order value). Management said it will consider reporting in crores for consistency.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a record order book and strong domestic traction. Management was cautious on FY28 growth and margins, using ranges and caveats, and was evasive on order-level price versus volume splits and market share, which it said it could not provide.
key_quotes: Overall, the quarter delivered strong growth across revenue and profitability, supported by a robust order book.
So, as far as the EBITDA margins are concerned, we should look at somewhere in the range of 19% to 21%.
We definitely would be growing between 10% to 15% next year, because of our new offerings, because of the demand of the output that gets developed, generated from our machines.
So, currently, it is very, I mean, minuscule. This year we expect that the total revenue from the recycling piece of machinery would be around in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

adds.what: New shed for additional assembly capacity (Kanpur land available for further expansion)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 30-35% (midpoint 32.5%), backed by a ~INR2,000 crore order book (+93% YoY), a current capacity ceiling of ~INR2,500 crore revenue, and INR75 crore FY27 capex, though the new shed has no stated timing and FY28 growth is guided down to 10-15%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides a sustainable EBITDA margin of 19-21% (internal 20%) versus 19.4% in Q2 and 20.7% a year earlier, and gross margin fell ~3% QoQ to ~41% on input cost inflation, so expansion above current levels is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New assembly shed and Kanpur land planned with no stated timing, and current capacity supports only ~INR2,500 crores revenue versus FY27 guidance implying ~INR2,300-2,400 crores, so balancing equipment is needed in one or two plants.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% with H2 at INR1,200-1,300 crores (vs H1 INR1,097 crores), backed by the ~INR2,000 crore order book, but FY28 growth is guided down to 10-15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of ~INR75 crores is already set for maintenance, balancing and new machine capacity, and utilisation cannot be measured precisely, so a further capacity capex announcement is plausible as FY28 demand sits near the INR2,500 crore ceiling.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Record order book of ~INR2,000 crores (+93% YoY) and inquiry pipeline of INR13,000 crores at 15-20% conversion support the 30-35% FY27 guide, and H2 is guided at INR1,200-1,300 crores, but capacity ceiling and price-lock contracts cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY28 growth already guided down to 10-15%, and commodity-led margin pressure (gross margin down ~3% QoQ, EBITDA margin 19.4% vs 20.7% YoY) and execution delays of 6-9 months could push revenue or margin below plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Recycling machinery is expected to double from INR30-35 crores in FY27 with ReclaMax 120 supplied, washing lines and mother-baby recycling launched, so new recycling product revenue is guided to scale.

rows.label: Order book held at INR2,000-2,200 crores by Mar 2027
rows.why: Order book is ~INR2,000 crores (+93% YoY, +12% QoQ) with management guiding the range to INR2,000-2,200 crores, against a INR13,000 crore pipeline at 15-20% conversion.

rows.label: Price increases flow through on new orders
rows.why: List prices were raised in February 2026 and July 2026, and orders booked after revisions are priced at new rates, though 6-9 month contracts carry no interim increase.

rows.label: Working capital cycle elevated
rows.why: Net working capital cycle rose to ~92 days from 84 days at end FY26, with customer advances at ~20% of order value supporting cash, so reversal depends on dispatch timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on record order book, domestic traction and FY27 30-35% growth, but cautious on FY28 growth of 10-15%, margins (19-21%) and commodity costs; analysts pressed on price versus volume splits and market share, which management declined to give.
